knownFor: חסיד דבבל — the pious one of Babylon (תענית כג:)
Greatly expanded the Sura academy: lectured through 13 amoraim (meturgemanim); ~800 disciples remained through the year (כתובות קו.)
Rose from extreme poverty to great wealth after Rav's blessing (once pawned his belt for kiddush wine) (מגילה כז:-כח.)
Worked his own land, watered his fields, gathered his own produce and herded his own animals (מגילה כח. / ירושלמי סנהדרין פ"א ה"א / כתובות קה.)
Devoted himself to sustaining the poor; each cloudy day rode out and repaired every collapsing wall, rebuilding at his own expense when owners could not (מגילה כז. / תענית כ:)
Wrote seventy (per Dikdukei Soferim: seven) Torah scrolls (ב"ב יד.)
Rav granted him authority to render legal rulings (רשות לדון) like a colleague (סנהדרין ה.)
ר"ה ראש לכל המטות — after R' Yochanan's death the sages of Eretz Yisrael too accepted him as their head; read among the kohanim though he was a Yisrael (חגיגה פ"א ה"ח / גיטין נט:)
His death was a mitat neshika (death by a kiss), having lived well beyond eighty (gevurot) (מו"ק כח.)
